events.title: The Sun King Is Born
events.description: Louis XIV of France was born at the Château de Saint-Germain-en-Laye. His parents were King Louis XIII and Anne of Austria. He became king at age four and reigned for 72 years, one of the longest reigns in European history.
events.significance: Louis XIV made France the leading power in Europe. His court at Versailles became the model of royal splendor, and his reign shaped European politics and culture.

events.title: First Continental Congress Convenes
events.description: Delegates from twelve of the thirteen American colonies gathered in Philadelphia. They met to coordinate a response to British colonial policies. Georgia did not send a delegate.
events.significance: The meeting was the first major step toward unified colonial government. It set the stage for the American Revolution and the creation of the United States.

events.title: Munich Olympics Hostage Crisis
events.description: Members of the Palestinian group Black September took eleven Israeli athletes and coaches hostage at the Olympic Village in Munich. The crisis ended in tragedy, and all the hostages were killed.
events.significance: The attack shocked the world and changed how international sporting events handle security. It also became a defining moment in the history of modern terrorism.

events.title: Voyager 1 Launches
events.description: NASA launched the Voyager 1 space probe from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on a Titan IIIE-Centaur rocket. It was sent to study Jupiter and Saturn.
events.significance: Voyager 1 later became the most distant human-made object from Earth. It entered interstellar space and still carries a message for any distant civilization that finds it.

events.title: Mother Teresa Dies in Calcutta
events.description: Mother Teresa died in Calcutta, India, at age 87. She had spent decades caring for the sick and the poor through the Missionaries of Charity, the order she founded.
events.significance: A Nobel Peace Prize winner, she became a global symbol of compassion and humanitarian service. The Catholic Church later declared her a saint.
